name_en: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

school_level.academic_text: Taught master’s other than EMBA (Graduate School): graduated from a recognised university and obtained a bachelor’s degree, normally with honours not lower than Second Class or achieving an average grade of not lower than “B”; or completed a course of study in a tertiary educational institution and obtained professional or similar qualifications equivalent to a bachelor’s degree. Business School master’s page: a bachelor’s degree with Second Class honours or an average grade of B from a recognised university, or professional qualifications equivalent to a bachelor’s degree. 2027 intake page: obtain a bachelor’s degree with at least second class honours or a grade B from a recognised university on or before 31 July 2027, or an equivalent professional qualification. EMBA is separately defined and does not use the Second Class / grade B rule.
school_level.english_text: Business School master’s page and Graduate School (applicants are told to use the Graduate School page for details): a degree from a university in Hong Kong or a degree programme whose medium of instruction was English; or TOEFL 79 of 120 / 4.5 of 6 (Internet-based/Home Edition); or IELTS (Academic) 6.5 (Test Centre based/Online); or GMAT Band 21 (Verbal); or GMAT Focus Edition Band 78 (Verbal); or a recognised professional qualification examined in English (programme discretion). Graduate School also accepts a pass in English in HKALE (AS Level), Hong Kong Higher Level Examination, CUHK Matriculation Examination, or GCE A-Level/AS-Level, or HKDSE English Language Level 4 or above. No IELTS subscore minimum and no CET are stated. The pages do not label the TOEFL 120-point and 6-point scales as before or after 21 January 2026. MBA, JD/MBA, EMBA (Chinese), FMBA and DBA (Chinese) state their own English rules.
school_level.gmat_gre_text: Two official wordings differ. Admission-requirements page: applicants to a full-time programme may be required to submit GMAT, GMAT Focus Edition or GRE; for part-time, a score is encouraged but not required. 2027 intake page: GMAT/GRE scores are not mandatory, but a good score will strengthen the application. Score reports are valid for five years from the test date. Online/at-home GMAT, GMAT Focus Edition or GRE General Test at Home may be recognised, subject to the programme. Priority is given to a recognised official score report. Individual programmes mostly say a score is not mandatory.
school_level.waiver_text: English is waived, without a test, for a Hong Kong university degree or an English-medium degree, and Graduate School may still ask for extra proof. A recognised professional qualification examined in English may be accepted at the programme’s discretion. GMAT Verbal Band 21 or GMAT Focus Edition Verbal Band 78 can itself satisfy the English minimum. TOEFL/IELTS valid for two years from the test date; GMAT / GMAT Focus Edition valid for five years. GMAT (Verbal) 21 is accepted until that score’s validity expires. CET is not mentioned.
